correctness.rationale: On the repaired finding, anchor one labeled point and order the other two: the uniform longitudes give joint half-gap density 2/pi². Using the tangent dot products, with X dot Y=1-2(1-k)sin²(a) and the two cyclic analogues, reduces the angle inequalities to the three cotangent products <k. These products sum to one. A nonpositive cotangent leaves exactly the other product potentially positive, and that product is at least one, so such a shape is never acute and cannot have two nonacute angles for k>0. On the positive simplex the inverse cotangents in the proof are positive with pair sum one and reproduce the unique angles with sum pi. In variables A=cot(a), B=cot(b), C=(1-AB)/(A+B), the determinant for (u,v)=(AB,BC) relative to (A,B) is 2ABC/(A+B); multiplying by (1+A²)(1+B²) and using AB+BC+CA=1 gives 2(1-u)(1-v)(1-s), establishing the claimed density. Integration over the levels gives the marginal and Q by w=(1-u)/(1+u); the inner overlap integral uses 1/((1-v)(u+v)) and yields exactly the logarithm stated. Differentiating Phi/2 gives log(u)/(1-u²) and differentiating H_k gives log(u+k)/(1-u²), so the given antiderivative and real arguments are valid. A pair of coordinates cannot both be >=1/2 because the third is positive, while for k<1/2 choosing u,v>k with u+v<1 gives positive mass. Triple failure is impossible for k>1/3, exactly the range where inclusion–exclusion is used. The quadratic central and edge triangles have coordinate areas (9/2)(k-1/3)² and (1-2k)²/2, with densities 27/(8pi²) and 4/pi² at the limiting points. Their analytic local expansions give continuous first derivatives and distinct second derivatives at the two transitions. The small-R series follows from w=R²/2+R⁴/12+O(R⁶) and the odd dilogarithm difference. It supplies examples and a numerical value only; the proof covers the continuum. Frozen verification code and notes were inspected, not executed.
